answer_1.quote: Automatic summarization has enjoyed renewed interest in recent years, thanks to the popularity of neural network models and their ability to learn continuous representations...

answer_2.quote: We evaluated summarization quality automatically using ROUGE... We report unigram and bigram overlap (ROUGE-1 and ROUGE-2) as a means of assessing informativeness and the longest common subsequence (ROUGE-L) as a means of assessing fluency... We also use FactCC to evaluate the factual correctness of the generated summaries.

answer_4.quote: In addition to automatic evaluation, we also assessed system output by eliciting human judgments... Evaluation was conducted on the Amazon Mechanical Turk crowdsourcing platform... For WikiCatSum... Crowdworkers were presented with the output of two systems...
answer_4.guideline: Participants decided which summary was better based on criteria: Succinctness (avoid repetition), Informativeness (capture important information), Fluency (fluent and grammatical). For WikiCatSum, outputs were compared based on information in the gold summary.
